brief_rationale: The trajectory completes all responsibility-chain items without any minor or serious error, and triggers four high-order points with meaningful impact. HO1 (patient-state-sensitive communication) is visible in plain-language explanations that separate symptom relief from kidney stability and reassure without promising dialysis. HO2 (real-world constraint navigation) appears when the model elicits the patient's fear of repeated blood draws, negotiates a minimum-visit same-day blood/urine testing plan, and provides caregiver language for the testing purpose. HO3 (patient-misinformation correction) occurs when the model corrects the specific misconception that reduced swelling after diuretics means kidney disease is better, using plain zh-CN and obtaining teach-back. HO4 (hidden-state discovery) is fulfilled by multiple workspace queries that uncover prior CKD4/diabetic nephropathy, urine ACR 128.4 mg/g, historical creatinine/eGFR trajectory, and follow-up gaps, which are then integrated into the urgency explanation. No important non-chain defect is present; closure is safe, executable, and traceable as valid_closure.
